faults.detail: At 360 px the game does not render: the screen is a static card reading "Fraction Slice / equal / fraction / piece / part" with no bar, no cut control and no instruction, so the piece cannot be played.

faults.where: piece-p412.png and piece-l1366.png, item label over the bar
faults.detail: The label "3 barabar parts" overlaps the tilted bar: the word "parts" runs across the bar's top edge (clearest at 1366 px). The text can still be read, but it overlaps.

Wave titled "Spot the whole" with sub "Teen equal pieces yaad rakho" contains the item {"parts": 4}. The instruction to remember three equal pieces contradicts a four-part cut, and the title does not match what the child does.

notes: The maths is correct (1/3, 2/3, 1/4, 1/2 cuts; equal parts). The equal-cut grading ("itna farq", "chhota piece") would show a child who holds the unequal-parts mix-up where it goes wrong. It fails because it does not render at 360 px, because a label overlaps the bar, and because wave 3's subtitle does not match its item.

faults.detail: At 360 px the game does not render: the screen is a static card reading "Landfall / line / equal / gaps / mark" with no number line or fraction, so the piece cannot be played.

faults.where: spec.waves[0] (title "Gaps gino", sub "Marks nahi, equal gaps gino", ticks 2, items "1/3", "1/3", "2/3"); visible on piece-p412.png / piece-l1366.png
faults.detail: The child is told to count equal gaps, but the line on screen is marked in halves (one middle mark, 2 gaps) while the fraction to catch is 1/3. Following the instruction gives halves, not thirds, so the marks do not let the child see that counting gaps is right and counting marks is wrong. The other waves do the same (ticks 4 with fifths, ticks 3 with quarters, ticks 7 on 0-2 with quarters). Wave 3's sub "3 marks ka matlab 4 gaps" also appears to sit on a line of 3 gaps, judging by how wave 1 draws ticks 2.

notes: Every graded target (1/3, 2/3, 1/5-4/5, 1/4-3/4, 5/4, 3/2, 7/4 on 0-2) is a correct position. The fault is that the marks shown never divide the line into the gaps the fractions need, so the gap-counting idea cannot be applied. The scaffoldTicks (correct counts) may appear after misses, but the first screen cannot show this.

faults.detail: At 360 px the game does not render: the screen is a static card reading "Landfall / size / bigger / strips / equal" with no number line or fraction, so the piece cannot be played.

notes: The content is sound: unit fractions 1/2, 1/3, 1/4, 1/6, 1/8 are placed one at a time on one 0-1 line, so 1/8 lands nearest 0. A child who thinks 1/8 > 1/4 would see the belief go wrong. The only failure is the missing render at 360 px; the 412 and 1366 px screens are clear. "Same pizza" on a number line is a slightly odd frame but not an error.

faults.detail: At 360 px the game does not render: the screen is a static card reading "Plot / perimeter / side / square / breadth" with no grid or goal, so the piece cannot be played.
The banner "Round 1/4  Stake exactly 40 sq units" is drawn over the coach line "Grid par plot claim karo", leaving only "Gr" and "o" showing on either side of the banner.
"Stake exactly 40 sq units": "stake" is not a plain word for a class 6 child and sits in English beside Hinglish coach text ("Grid par plot claim karo").

notes: The maths and the design are good: area 40 (e.g. 8x5, perimeter 26) is followed by perimeter 26 with "is baar nayi shape", which shows a child who multiplies for perimeter that the same perimeter can enclose a different area. Area 49 and perimeter 20 fit the 15x10 grid. It fails on the missing render at 360 px, the banner overlap at 1366 px, and the word "stake".
